open_points.subject: canonical operation catalogue shared by dispatch and service rights
open_points.text: “The operation table: every operation of either surface” and “not which service may call it, which is the release's table alone”; also, “the owner's operations are the owner interface's.”
open_points.question: Which module owns the canonical identities and complete set of operations, including their surface, so that `operations`, `release_declarations`/`service_access`, and `owner_interface` cannot define different operation sets or names?
options: `operations` owns the canonical catalogue and the other modules reference its operation identities
`release_declarations` owns service-operation identities while `owner_interface` separately owns owner-operation identities
`models` owns a common operation vocabulary referenced by all three
open_points.default_guess: Make `operations` own the canonical catalogue and require the release rights table and owner-interface routes to reference its operation identities.

open_points.subject: placement of the answer disclosure-class check
open_points.text: The shared check-order passage says “`operations` never re-orders them and adds no check of its own after stage (2),” while the answer passage says “`operations` computes an answer's class as the highest of its facts' and refuses the answer whole when it is above the caller's highest,” and `operations` owns “A09 rule 4 at the call.”
open_points.question: Is the disclosure-class refusal a stage-(1) authorization check performed before record processing, or a separate check after stages (3)–(6); if it is later, must a state-changing transaction be rolled back when it fails?
options: Determine the operation's maximum answer class at stage (1) and refuse before domain work
Compute the actual answer class after stages (3)–(6), but before committing any change
Treat the class check as an explicitly permitted post-stage check, with separately stated commit semantics
open_points.default_guess: Check the declared maximum output class at stage (1), and retain a pre-commit assertion that the actual answer does not exceed it.

set_aside.unit: 30_modules.md:Facts several modules touch, and their one owner: Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
set_aside.subject: transaction and snapshot boundary for read operations
set_aside.text: “Every action is one call of `operations` and, when it changes the store, one store transaction”; later, “Every agent-authority call takes it too, a read included.”
set_aside.question: Do non-agent reads run in one `store` read transaction/snapshot, especially reads that assemble several records, and is `operations` responsible for opening that transaction?
options: Every operation uses one store transaction; writes and agent reads additionally take the write lock
Only agent-authority reads are transactionally ordered; other reads may perform independent store reads
Only reads that join or assemble multiple records use one read transaction
set_aside.default_guess: Run every store-backed operation in one snapshot transaction, with changes and all agent-authority calls additionally serialized as stated.

witness.initial: An active project has one room and Client Portal may read its project card while the owner anonymises the project.
events: Client Portal begins `read a project` and reads the Project record.
The owner confirms anonymisation; `operations` removes the project's identifying facts and rooms in its transaction.
Client Portal reads the rooms needed for the same project-card answer.
outcomes: With one read snapshot, Client Portal receives either the complete pre-anonymisation card or the erased answer.
With independent reads, Client Portal can combine the pre-anonymisation Project read with the post-anonymisation empty room set, or otherwise produce a mixed-time answer.

set_aside.unit: 30_modules.md:Facts several modules touch, and their one owner: Facts several modules touch, and their one owner
set_aside.subject: secret and owner-session-value non-disclosure invariant
set_aside.text: “No module puts a secret, a confirmation value, a CSRF value or an owner session's identity into a record, a log line, a diagnostic, an audit entry, a URL or the data of an answer.”
set_aside.question: Which module owns enforcement of this cross-cutting non-disclosure rule across diagnostics, audit construction, HTTP answers, URLs, and persistence?
options: Each producing module owns the prohibition for its own outputs
A single diagnostics/serialization boundary owns redaction and rejection
`operations` owns validation of all records and answers while transport and startup modules separately own URLs and diagnostics
set_aside.default_guess: Assign each output boundary responsibility for never accepting these values, with typed secret/session values that cannot be serialized by the ordinary record, diagnostic, audit, URL, or answer paths.
